task.description: Extend test coverage for the §2.2 delta added since your original test file was written. The security-critical property added in this rework is the one-way gate: Letflow.Identity.sync_role_claims_from_token/3 seeds group_members from JWT claims ONLY when a user's role_claims_synced_at is nil, and must NEVER re-fire once set -- meaning a revoked-then-still-claiming user's access must NOT silently resurrect on a later login/token refresh. Your original test file (test/letflow/plugs/iss0736_oidc_live_revocation_test.exs) proves the live-check-on-next-request property but was written against a fixture that pre-seeded group_members directly, sidestepping the sync path entirely. Add a NEW test (in the same file or a new one under test/letflow/) that: (1) simulates a first-ever OIDC login for a brand-new user whose JWT claims a real recognized role (e.g. PROCESS_OPERATOR) with NO pre-existing group_members row -- assert the sync fires, group_members gets a row, role_claims_synced_at gets stamped, and the request succeeds with that role; (2) simulates the tenant_admin revoking that role (Identity.remove_group_member/3) -- assert immediate 403 on retry with the same JWT (same property as the original test, now via the real sync path); (3) simulates that SAME user hitting the pipeline AGAIN with the SAME (still role-claiming) JWT after revocation -- assert the sync does NOT re-fire (role_claims_synced_at unchanged, no new group_members row, still 403) -- this is the critical regression-proof for the one-way gate. Run all new tests and quote real pass output. Run everything in the foreground -- no background Monitor waiting.
acceptance_criteria: New test proves the sync-on-first-login path (not just pre-seeded fixtures)
New test proves the one-way gate specifically: sync does not re-fire after revocation even though the JWT still claims the role
Real quoted test output showing all pass
No product code changed -- test files only
